headline: Bitcoin starts the week near $65,000 after falling about 12% last week, with fear at extreme levels and money still leaving crypto funds before a busy week of Fed news, Nvidia results and Anthropic's share listing.

market.asOf: Read at about 23:55 UTC Sun 15 Nov (06:55 Bangkok Mon) from CoinMarketCap coin pages; CoinGecko pages could not be opened this run. Prices move fast; use the live prices on this page.
market.fearGreed: Extreme fear: the Alternative.me Crypto Fear & Greed Index read 10 out of 100 (Extreme Fear), down from 13 a day earlier and 28 a week ago.

stories.title: Bitcoin starts a new week near $65,000 after a weekend low near $62,000
stories.summary: Bitcoin fell to about $62,000 late on Saturday (US time), its lowest in three to four months depending on the source, as traders who had borrowed to bet on higher prices were forced out. It bounced about 5% and held in the mid-$60,000s through Sunday. The week opened near $74,800, so this is a weekly loss of about 12-13%. CME bitcoin futures reopen as the new week starts.
points: The overnight low was $61,946 on Coinbase and the week opened at $74,757, per CryptoTicker; Bybit's low was $61,899.20, per Blockchain Reporter.
Bitcoin was at $65,071 at 23:27 UTC Sunday, about 5.13% above that low, per Blockchain Reporter; Cointelegraph's weekly roundup had it down 12.4% on the week at $65,116.
Ether fell 14.4% on the week to $1,822, per Cointelegraph, after dropping as low as $1,715, its lowest since July, per CryptoTicker.
About $1.96B of crypto bets were force-closed (liquidated) in 24 hours, per CoinGlass data cited by crypto.news; CryptoTicker counted over $2B.
Funding rates on bitcoin perpetual futures stayed negative on Binance and OKX, meaning traders betting on lower prices are paying those betting on higher prices, per Blockchain Reporter.

stories.title: Money keeps leaving crypto ahead of a heavy week: the Fed, Nvidia and Anthropic's IPO
stories.summary: US spot bitcoin ETFs, the way many Americans hold bitcoin in a brokerage account, had seven straight days of withdrawals through Friday, and stablecoin supply is shrinking, which means less ready cash to buy. Futures traders expect the Fed to raise rates in December; that is a market bet, not a Fed decision. ETF flows resume with US trading on Monday.
points: Spot bitcoin ETFs lost about $2.35B over two weeks: $1.07B this past week and $1.28B the week before, per Cointelegraph.
Friday 13 November alone saw $185.4M leave, $143.5M of it from BlackRock's IBIT, per Farside data cited by crypto.news.
Investors pulled $398.9M from US ether funds between 9 and 13 November, and USDT, USDC and DAI supply fell a record $11.5B in 30 days, per CryptoTicker citing Coinbase Institutional.
From 11 to 14 November, net aggressive selling was 7,438 BTC on a major unnamed US-dollar exchange versus 2,707 BTC on Binance, per Binance Research cited by crypto.news.
CME FedWatch showed an 88.5% chance of a December rate hike on Saturday, per CryptoTicker.

sources.label: CryptoTicker: ether funds, stablecoins, Fed odds

stories.title: Big corporate bitcoin holders under pressure: Saylor hints at a buy as end-of-November deadlines approach
stories.summary: Strategy chairman Michael Saylor posted "This dip could use a little orange," a style of post that has often come before a purchase, but nothing is confirmed until the company discloses a buy. Strategy's bitcoin is now worth less than it paid. Two deadlines on 30 November matter: MSCI removes Strategy from its indexes, and Trump Media's noteholders can ask for cash for $1B of notes.
points: Strategy holds 850,364 BTC bought for about $64.16B, an average of $75,456 each; its last disclosed buy was 1,036 BTC at $79,012 each, per crypto.news.
That leaves an unrealized loss of about $8.46B, and each $1,000 move in bitcoin changes the holding's value by about $850M, per Bloomingbit.
MSCI removes Strategy from its USA index and Metaplanet from its Japan small-cap index after the close on 30 November, per The Block.
Miner MARA sold 13,597 BTC for about $1.1B and used $750M to repay loans backed by bitcoin, per crypto.news.
Trump Media noteholders can demand cash for its $1B of notes from 30 November; the company moved about 4,259 BTC from wallets tagged as note collateral to Crypto.com on 5 November, per Parameter.

briefs.title: US crypto market-structure bill stalls for 2026
briefs.summary: The CLARITY Act is stuck after a 49-50 Senate vote in September (60 needed); a Senate Banking hearing on two SEC nominees is set for 19 November at 10am ET, per crypto.news.

briefs.title: Senator calls for probe of the CFTC and Kalshi
briefs.summary: Sen. Blumenthal wants Congress to look into alleged collusion between the US futures regulator and prediction market Kalshi over stock perpetual approvals, per Bloomingbit.

briefs.title: US moves to seize or freeze more than $1.2B stolen in the Binance hack
briefs.summary: The Justice Department says it got court approval to seize or restrain more than $1.2B and attributes the 29 October theft of more than $6B to North Korea.

briefs.title: Binance's ether reserves at lowest since 2021
briefs.summary: About 2.9M ETH sits on Binance, the lowest since 2021, per CryptoQuant data cited by The Crypto Basic.

briefs.title: Korean exchange Coinone discloses a customer-data breach
briefs.summary: Customer data was exposed through its contractor MetaM in a 12 November intrusion; Coinone says its trading and wallet systems were not breached, per The Crypto Basic.

briefs.title: Zcash holders vote on a dev-fund treasury from Monday
briefs.summary: Voting runs 16-30 November, with options including moving 50,000 ZEC or dissolving the fund, per CryptoTicker.

briefs.title: A bigger bitcoin options expiry lands on 27 November
briefs.summary: About 88,000 BTC of options expire on Friday 27 November, far more than this Friday's weekly expiry, per BigGo Finance.
